title: pm/fleet-write: advisory_read holds its sender to target-write, by the maintainer's ruling, since the collaborator gate refuses every live read
body:
domain:skills#2 · os-justin · session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj

## What

`advisory_read` (the sealed advisory read, #29420, landed in #29536) holds the sender to `senderGate: 'collaborator'` in `scripts/pm/fleet-write/ops.mjs`. The maintainer has ruled it becomes `'target-write'`, the gate every other relay row keeps.

## The ruling

The maintainer, in session `session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj` on 2026-11-02, answering the seat's question whether the read's sender gate should change from collaborator to write on the target repository, verbatim:

> 同意改成对仓库有写权限,立卡派发修复

This settles the open question the #29420 os-dev report left for the maintainer (comment 6584655262, `open_questions[0]`, options A collaborator / B target-write). The ruling is B.

## The measurement that prompted it (the first live reads, 2026-11-02)

- `advisory_collaborators_add` for the sender landed, and its PATCH answer lists the sender among the collaborators (run 41545025429).
- Three `advisory_read` strokes after it, on two advisories, were each refused at fence `sender` ("is not a collaborator on it"): runs 41545143476, 41545259848, 41546082963.
- A re-sent `advisory_collaborators_add` on one of those advisories was a no-op: its pre-PATCH GET, under the write grant, already lists the sender (run 41546190167).
- So the write-grant GET lists the sender in `collaborating_users`, and the read-grant GET the fence judges does not. Why the read-grant answer omits it is **unverified** (a hypothesis: the platform withholds `collaborating_users` from a read-only grant).
- A sender with write on the target can already add itself to any advisory whose id it holds (`ops.mjs`, the sender-gate paragraph above `advisory_read`), so the collaborator gate excluded no one; it only blocked every live read.

## Acceptance

- `advisory_read`'s `senderGate` is `'target-write'`; the header prose and the row comment record the ruling verbatim, in place of "the card's recommendation" and "the maintainer rules which stands, on the pull request".
- The relay self-tests that pin the default gate move with it; an unknown gate still fails closed.
- After merge, one live `advisory_read` by a seat with write on the target opens (the seat runs it; recorded here as a run id, no advisory id).

## Out of bounds

- ⛔ The row's `grant` stays `read`. If a read under the read grant is refused once the gate is switched, that is a fork for the maintainer, never a raise to write.
- ⛔ No advisory text, id or mechanism in the PR, the commits or the changeset.
